segments.text: Hi, I'm Jennifer Evangelista, a data engineering and solutions architecture specialist from Brazil. In one minute, here is the idea behind Shield.

A scheduler can tell you that every job succeeded. It cannot tell you that the jobs processed the right day. A backfill that finishes this morning still belongs to last week, and a gate that only checks today's runs lets it through.

So the gate asks a different question. Every run records the business date it processed and its attempt number. The newest attempt wins. And a date is ready only when every required job succeeded for the date the report needs.

A check is only half the answer, because someone still has to decide what happens next. Shield scans, explains the impact, names the owners and proposes a fix. A person approves, edits or rejects it in the chat. Shield applies only what was approved, checks again, and writes everything to an audit trail.

Switch is what makes that a team workflow. It turns the channel into a room, decides who can talk to Shield, carries each decision with the person's name, and keeps the audit document where the whole team can see it.
Checks by Shield. Decisions by people. In the chat your team already uses.
